issues.description: Ambiguous/overloaded meaning of the `num_qubits` parameter for create_single_qubit_gate: the problem statement and the template describe create_single_qubit_gate(num_qubits, target, gate_matrix) where `num_qubits` is documented as “the number of qubits in the system” (i.e., the total system size). However, the provided reference solution (and its implementation of create_controlled_single_qubit_gate) calls create_single_qubit_gate with a smaller integer (the control index) to construct sub-block identity/DD components (e.g., id_path = create_single_qubit_gate(control, 0, np.identity(...))). This effectively treats `num_qubits` as the size of a sub-system/block rather than the full system size. The mismatch in intended meaning can confuse students implementing create_controlled_single_qubit_gate: they may assume `num_qubits` must always be the global N and attempt to call create_single_qubit_gate with the full system size, producing a different DD construction or failing to follow the solution approach.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter semantics explicit and consistent. Two possible fixes: (A) Clarify the docstring for create_single_qubit_gate to state that the first argument is the number of qubits of the (sub-)system being constructed (i.e., it can be used to build smaller identity/gate blocks), and add an explanatory example showing calls with smaller values when building controlled gates; or (B) keep create_single_qubit_gate strictly scoped to the full-system size (num_qubits = N) and modify create_controlled_single_qubit_gate in the template (and solution) to explicitly build the required identity sub-blocks (e.g., by a small helper create_identity_block(k) or by using make_dd loops) instead of calling create_single_qubit_gate with a non-global `num_qubits`. Either approach removes the unintended parameter-semantic overload and prevents student confusion.
